matt.h: Heads-up — since last night's batch window we've seen a cluster of GPU allocations stuck in PROVISIONING in us-west2. Symptoms point to local NVMe saturation but it's not the usual scrub/backlog spike.
anya: saw the alert. any logs?
matt.h: attaching a quick `iostat` snapshot from one affected host — read/write wait jumping to 300-800ms, util ~99%. Also `dmesg` shows repeated `CRC error` on nvme0n1 at offsets that look like small-block hotspots.
matt.h: ```
avg-cpu:  %user   %nice %system %iowait  %steal   %idle
          12.3    0.0    8.7   42.1     0.0   37.0
Device             tps    MB_read/s    MB_wrtn/s   await  r_await  w_await
nvme0n1          1200        80.5         40.2     620   210      810
```
jordan: interesting — not a scrub backlog spike? how's the janitor queue?
matt.h: janitor backlog is slightly elevated but not enough to explain sustained high await. The weird bit is we see lots of tiny 4KB writes in hotspots (probably model shard checkpoint churn + tempfiles). Drives are showing fragmentation of free extents and CRCs on small blocks.
katie: could be an overlayfs/metadata amplification case. We had a rollout on the scratch cleaner last week — any correlation?
matt.h: rollouts didn't overlap timewise, but config change reduced coalescing window which may increase small writes. I suspect microfragmentation -> write amplification -> SMART errors exposing slow retry paths.
anya: do we have SMART logs?
jordan: grabbed `smartctl -a` from a node — reallocated sector count still 0 but UDMA_CRC_Error_Count increased and some vendor OOS counters ticked. Not full failure yet.
katie: from a mitigation POV: we can (1) throttle checkpoint frequency for batch jobs, (2) throttle janitor concurrency to reduce interleaving, (3) move provisioning to alternate storage-class nodes. Cost/throughput tradeoffs obvious.
matt.h: propose immediate triage: 1) block new on-demand GPU allocs onto nodes with `ssd-scratch:high-iops` label, 2) enable conservative coalescing on overlayfs for next 6h, 3) increase fstrim cadence on affected pools, 4) kill/recover a small set for observation.
anya: +1 for redirecting new allocs. how many nodes have the `high-iops` tag in us-west2?
jordan: ~15 nodes. Should handle current backpressure, but won't scale long term.
sre-bot: deploy-trigger: routing-policy patch applied to allocation service — tag filter `ssd-scratch:high-iops` set for us-west2.
katie: also recommend we temporarily disable the cleaner's sample-based aggressive delete; it creates lots of tiny metadata churn when it races with batch checkpoints.
matt.h: we ran a local profiler — pattern looks like repeated `fallocate(1)` + small overwrites. Could try switching to write-through tempfiles to reduce metadata churn.
anya: risk of data loss? for tempfiles it's fine. For checkpoints we should coordinate with jobs team.
jordan: I'll open a quick API patch to prefer `--checkpoint-reduce-frequency` for the nightly batch job set.
katie: what about a longer-term fix? drive firmware team has suggested vendor patch that reduces small-write retry amplification but it's disruptive.
matt.h: long-term: (A) move to larger aggregate scratch devices per host to reduce fragmentation, (B) vendor firmware update in maintenance window, (C) smarter coalescing in the janitor and checkpointer.
anya: can we do a canary in eu-west1 first (less pressure)
jordan?: typo on my name, ignore.
jordan: yes — schedule firmware canary for eu-west1 next Tue night. I'll coordinate with hw-maint team.
sre-bot: incident-note: temporary routing applied, janitor concurrency lowered to 2 in us-west2, checkpoint frequency reduced for nightly-batch to 1/3rd cadence.
matt.h: monitoring checklist — track nvme await, CRC error counts, janitor queue depth, gpu provision latency. If Await stays >300ms after 2h we escalate to forced migration.
katie: I'll add dashboards and alert thresholds.
anya: thanks — let's reconvene in 2h. :thumbsup:
matt.h: thanks all, will post updates in thread.
